primitives.name: Legal Boundary Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: Do not launch paid contests, prizes, deposits, payouts, live leaderboards, sportsbook/DFS affiliate flows, or real-money entries without founder/legal approval.
primitives.assumptions: All monetary and real-time features require explicit legal approval.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when unauthorized financial flows are enabled.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's legal risk inference model where MEDIUM risk triggers conditional flagging.
layer2.telemetry: Compliance flag status and approval timestamp

primitives.name: Data Boundary Isolation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Do not import real friend-history data without explicit consent and deletion controls.
primitives.assumptions: Real user data must be isolated and deleted upon request.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when real data is imported without consent.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSE's data integrity kernel enforcing fake-data-only mode.
layer2.telemetry: Data source origin and consent log

primitives.name: Feature Flag State Machine
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Feature flag disabled by default if code is ever approved.
primitives.assumptions: Feature activation requires explicit enablement and audit trail.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when feature is enabled without approval.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's runtime state machine that enforces disabled-by-default behavior.
layer2.telemetry: Feature flag toggle state and activation log

The legal boundary prevents unauthorized monetization; the data boundary isolates real-world data; and the feature flag ensures controlled rollout. Failure modes arise from bypassing any layer, leading to regulatory breach, data leak, or unintended exposure. The system's robustness depends on cross-layer vetoes ensuring no leakage between domains.
